test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 8 Mar 2021 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: In India, impeachment process is NOT applicable to _____ for removal from office.
solution:
The correct answer is __**the Prime Minister**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In India, the impeachment process is applicable to the President, Chief Justice of India, and Supreme Court Judges but not to the Prime Minister.
 
• The Prime Minister can be removed by a vote of no confidence in the Lok Sabha, rather than through impeachment.
 
• The President of India can be impeached for violation of the Constitution as per Article 61 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• Supreme Court Judges, including the Chief Justice of India, can be removed by impeachment for proven misbehavior or incapacity as per Article 124(4) of the Indian Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Impeachment Process**

 
 
• The impeachment process is a formal procedure used to remove high-ranking officials from office for misconduct or violation of the Constitution.
 
• In India, this process is detailed in Articles 61 and 124 of the Indian Constitution for the President and Supreme Court Judges respectively.
 
• For the President, either House of Parliament can initiate the impeachment process by leveling charges, which must be signed by at least one-fourth of the total members of that House.
 
• For Supreme Court Judges, the process involves a detailed investigation by a committee formed by the Parliament, and the motion for removal must be passed by both Houses of Parliament with a two-thirds majority.
 
 
 
• **Vote of No Confidence**
 
 
• A Vote of No Confidence is a parliamentary motion used to remove the Prime Minister and the Council of Ministers from office.
 
• If a majority of members in the Lok Sabha (the lower house of India's Parliament) vote against the Prime Minister, they must resign.
 
• This mechanism ensures that the Prime Minister retains the confidence of the majority of the Lok Sabha members to govern.
 
 
 
• **Chief Justice of India and Supreme Court Judges Removal**
 
 
• The removal process for Supreme Court Judges, including the Chief Justice of India, is outlined in Article 124(4) of the Constitution.
 
• Judges can be removed on grounds of "proven misbehavior" or "incapacity".
 
• The process involves a detailed investigation by a committee of three judges of the Supreme Court, a judge of a High Court, and a distinguished jurist.
 
• If the charges are substantiated, the motion for removal must be passed by both Houses of Parliament with a two-thirds majority of those present and voting.
